text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Tuesday as reported by the official Algerian news agency APS. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Eight days ahead of referendum to change the constitution, the authorities are getting ready especially in the southern regions where people will vote three days earlier.
- A total of 25,000 state-subsidised houses will be distributed soon.
- About 350,000 workers in cash-strapped state-owned companies are without pay.

- Air Algerie resumes flights to Paris airport before summer of 1997. The national airline had suspended flights to the French capital since June 1995 in a row with French aviation authorities over terminal change prompted by security concern.
- Following horror of mass slaughter of civilians by armed groups, people in the mountainous Chrea area abandon their villagers. "We must flee...flee," they said.
- Western and Arab security services draw up a black list of organisations, banks and Arab businessmen who finance "terrorist" organisations in Algeria, Egypt, Sudan and Jordan.
